rows.purpose: Open or resume a usable workspace with a verified full-model state and saved work context.
rows.reason: F-SESSION needs direct resume, and charter sections 4 and 5 require one new application and one entry path; the launch purpose survives while the retained runtime and G1/G2 doors are replaced.
requirements: Adopt coherent state, workspace and protection revisions and verify model identity before enabling puzzle input.
Open the full 600-cell-Full model with all 259,800 labels and 1,200 generators; a reduced introductory display must not reduce the model.
Resume saved context through the six layers, with asynchronous readiness and actionable startup errors.
rows.notes: Source-only proposal: no Windows, DirectX, input-device or performance behaviour was run. The U6-038 open candidate concerns operation controls rather than the launch purpose.

rows.purpose: Find every available command, its current meaning and its requirements, and invoke an explicitly chosen action.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 E5 require keyboard access to every action through the command table, including commands not yet disclosed by the learning path.
requirements: List every surviving command with its engine-reported availability, context and effective binding; explain unavailable actions.
Invoke the same command ID and gates as any other input route, rechecking the captured context before a mutation.
Soft key disclosure must never remove commands from the palette.

rows.purpose: Choose the orbit to work on while retaining the context of unfinished work in other orbits.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 2 and 4.2 require orbit-first work and deliberate orbit changes; charter section 5 replaces the old selector interaction.
requirements: Switch the session orbit and saved workspace context atomically; a failed switch must leave both unchanged.
Restore drafts and choices, resolve identities again and invalidate execution permission without rolling back current global protection.
Explain the certified collateral-dependent stage order without treating orbit ID order as that order or forcing a choice.

rows.purpose: Reach the actions appropriate to the inspected work object without re-entering its identity.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE need piece-focused context, and solving-workflow section 4.3 separates inspection from assigning roles or turning.
requirements: Preserve the canonical selection when focusing actions and display the object to which those actions apply.
Route each chosen action through the command table with current availability; opening actions must not assign roles or execute.
Provide a keyboard route even when no graphical object can receive focus.

rows.purpose: Bind and inspect the working piece, its exact destination arrangement and the fixed buffer positions A and B.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-FIND use these shared roles, and solving-workflow sections 3.1 and 4 require a buffer position to remain distinct from its changing occupant.
requirements: Use canonical identity and position IDs and explicit ordered target slots; matching colours do not establish the required arrangement.
Role assignment requires acknowledged actual-state inspection or validated explicit IDs; a forecast token cannot authorize capture of current state.
Share roles between Global, Local and tools at one revision; invalidate reviews on any role or target edit.
A focus that changes orbit must save context atomically, and inspecting a role must not reassign it.

rows.purpose: Find contextual explanations of commands, solving skills and the mathematical terms currently in use.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and charter section 5 D7, M4 and M6 require task-led teaching; the owner's 2 October scope decision limits theory to what the 1.0 interface actually shows.
requirements: Link command help and term cards to the current task, the shared glossary and reproducible diagrams from real geometry.
Define every displayed term, symbol and relation and supply a proof or cited proof only for facts on which interface correctness relies.
Keep help local, searchable and keyboard accessible, with human-reviewed English wording and the context-dependent trial text budgets.
Explain setup search separately from forbidden solving-macro generation; learning never unlocks execution privileges.
rows.notes: The U6-043 candidate is dialog dismissal, a different purpose from learning.

rows.purpose: Choose and revisit an explicit keyboard set suited to the current orbit and task.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 preserve explicit key-set switching, while charter section 5 E5 leaves final bindings to the new keyboard model.
requirements: Display the active set, effective bindings and affected canonical caps before input; camera, filter and piece motion must not silently change a key.
Retain explicit orbit/task sets and previous-set recall without prescribing 0.4 names, keys or slot counts.
Clear held Grip and Twist state on a set change and keep all 1,200 legal generators reachable.

rows.purpose: Inspect identities, fixed positions and exact slot correspondences while keeping the chosen work object in focus.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK need exact object and frame inspection; charter section 5 D8 and the owner's encoding decision move that purpose into the linked Global and Local views.
requirements: Distinguish fixed position, its occupant, physical identity and forecast identity using canonical IDs and the shared encoding grammar.
Keyboard navigation, hover, inspection, action opening and dismissal must not assign roles, select a Grip or execute a turn.
Bind correspondence diagrams to the displayed model, source, frame and revision; show chronological source-to-destination slot mappings with full exact details.
Wait for the matching inspection acknowledgment before enabling object actions and reject forecast-based current-state capture.
Present this information in the two linked views; retain exact details and focus when an expanded inspection is dismissed.

rows.purpose: Learn and use the effective keyboard meanings through an accessible onscreen representation.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-LEARN need discoverable Grip, Twist and command meanings; charter section 5 E5 and the owner's soft-disclosure decision preserve this purpose in the new shell.
requirements: F-04: Suspend presentation updates and key repaint work while the onscreen keyboard is hidden; refresh from current revisions when shown.
Show current bank, command contexts, canonical caps, ordered frames, legal Twist directions and effective binding overrides.
Onscreen and physical input must invoke identical command IDs and gates; inspecting a key must not invoke it.
Offer all commands through the palette and an explicit show-all disclosure choice; undisclosed keys must not become inaccessible.
Clear held input when focus or visibility changes and keep mathematical key meanings stable under camera and filter changes.

rows.purpose: Transfer a validated keyboard configuration without silently overwriting unrelated solving work.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-NAVIGATE require durable personalized input; command-table sections 1 and 2 require a checked file and explicit replacement scope through one command path.
requirements: Use a versioned bounded format, validate the complete configuration before saving and show shared/per-set replacement and inherited-default scope.
Apply only the inspected content digest against a current configuration revision, with explicit replacement consent and recoverable workspace changes.
Publish exports atomically and leave macros, frames, captures, roles, drafts and puzzle state unchanged by binding-only replacement.
Reject command/Grip/Twist conflicts and report typed errors without discarding the inspected input.

rows.purpose: Customize command, Grip and Twist bindings with clear conflict and replacement feedback.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 E5 require an efficient configurable keyboard workflow; command-table contexts and repeat rules govern the redesigned editor.
requirements: Capturing a chord must not invoke it; editors, modal tools and IME input must own their keystrokes.
Validate effective per-set and shared bindings before an atomic save, reject illegal physical-turn conflicts and require explicit replacement of another command.
Keep command IDs independent of physical keys and update all visible effective-key hints from the accepted configuration revision.
Provide workspace recovery for binding changes and retain unsaved input after validation or save failure.

rows.purpose: Choose whether a Grip remains selected while held or until explicitly released.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE need predictable physical input, and solving-workflow section 4.3 preserves explicit Grip selection while 1.0 redesigns its interaction.
requirements: Show the active input policy and selected canonical cap; changing policy must not issue a turn.
Clear held or latched input safely on focus loss, modal entry, busy state and bank/frame changes.
Reject ambiguous simultaneous Grip keys and apply the same meaning to physical and onscreen input.

rows.purpose: Select a legal cap and explicitly enter a turn in its fixed frame.
rows.reason: Solving-workflow section 4.3 treats selecting a Grip and applying a Twist as distinct actions; F-COMPOSE uses both, while only the Twist can serve F-EXECUTE.

parts.purpose: Select or release an explicitly identified cap without moving the puzzle.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE require deliberate Grip selection with stable mathematical meaning under solving-workflow section 4.3.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Show the selected canonical cap and ordered frame, honor the chosen hold/latch policy and reject ambiguous selection.
Keep all 1,200 generators accessible across explicit mappings; a bank slot limit must not limit the mechanical generator set.
Selection alone must not append a draft turn or change committed state.

parts.purpose: Apply one solver-requested legal turn to the chosen draft phase or the live puzzle.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE require explicit physical turns, with the draft/live and protection boundaries of solving-workflow section 4.1.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Resolve a legal generator from the explicit cap and ordered frame, carry state/frame guards and preserve chronological source-to-destination semantics.
Draft input changes only its phase; a live turn is a complete protected operation and cannot borrow a future Cleanup.
Suppress repeat, busy, modal and editor input and require an explicit solver action for every live turn.
Retain the accepted command receipt across refresh failure and never report an applied turn as rejected.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Remember, locate and deliberately activate the physical identity chosen as the next target.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow sections 3.3 and 4.2 give locked Next priority while keeping it a solver choice rather than automatic execution.
requirements: Store Next as a canonical physical identity, resolve its current position again after state changes and keep it distinct from protection.
Require explicit replacement, clearing and activation; locating must not replace Current or execute.
Activation into another orbit must save and restore per-orbit context atomically without reverting global protection or reusing an old review.

rows.purpose: Use pointer input to inspect a sticker or request a legal turn.
rows.reason: Solving-workflow section 4.3 separates inspection from turning, so F-FIND and F-EXECUTE require separate decisions despite the shared native mouse handler.

parts.purpose: Request a legal turn from an explicit pointer gesture on the puzzle.
parts.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-COMPOSE retain deliberate pointer turns, while charter sections 2 and 4 replace the retained runtime with a renderer that cannot mutate the model.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Convert the pick and explicit gesture into a command using the current state, cap and frame; the renderer must never perform scratch mechanical turns.
Apply the same draft/live, protection, busy and repeat rules as keyboard Twist input and preserve all collateral labels.
Keep accepted receipts across refresh/device failure and redraw from authoritative committed state; guard recovery so publication cannot remain held.

parts.purpose: Inspect the actual object corresponding to a current sticker hit without turning it.
parts.reason: F-FIND and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain inspection as a separate action; charter section 4 gives picking to the renderer and interpretation to the layers above.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Return a canonical sticker hit tied to the displayed model and revision, honoring interactive work scope and noninteractive references.
Inspection must not assign Current, a destination, a Grip or a camera position and must never commit a turn.
Withdraw stale hits after state, filter or device changes and use the same acknowledged object context as keyboard inspection.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Adjust workspace visibility and focus to work comfortably without losing the solving context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE preserves visibility and focus control; charter section 5 D8 and the owner's two-view decision replace the old collection of supporting windows.
requirements: Fullscreen changes and collapsing optional tools must preserve shared work context, camera state and keyboard reachability.
Keep Global and Local visible together in the workspace; hiding old supporting windows becomes management of optional tools rather than removal of either required view.
Clear held input before transferring focus and restore usable bounds on the current display without touching puzzle state.

rows.purpose: Access linked geometric views and position their cameras for the current work.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE need the two linked views, while F-NAVIGATE needs independent camera control; charter section 5 D8 keeps those purposes in a new host.

parts.purpose: Compare the piece and target locally while locating their relationship on the whole polytope.
parts.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE are the two view questions in charter section 5 D8 and the owner's 2 October two-view decision.
requirements: Global and Local must be visible together and share one context and revision, with no separate third puzzle or Hub view.
Local must compare actual and target ordered frames with fixed anchors; Global must locate canonical cells and their real relationships.
View focus and tool dismissal must preserve roles, protection and full-operation effects, including collateral outside filters.

parts.purpose: Rotate, zoom, reset or explicitly center geometric views without changing the work bindings.
parts.reason: F-NAVIGATE supports F-FIND and F-RELATE, and solving-workflow section 4.3 separates camera movement from inspection, targeting and Grip assignment.
requirements: Provide keyboard and pointer routes to named camera commands with bounded readable zoom and correct canonical center resolution.
Camera commands must not mutate or relabel mechanical state, change a key's cap/frame meaning or reassign solving roles.
Center-on-piece must resolve the current identity location; center-on-Grip must use the explicitly selected cap.
Keep camera work asynchronous where engine queries are needed and preserve legibility and picking at the current display scale.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Inspect geometric cells and deliberately move the camera to a selected cell.
rows.reason: F-RELATE uses cell inspection, and F-NAVIGATE uses camera positioning; solving-workflow section 4.3 requires those actions to remain separate.

parts.purpose: Read a selected or hovered cell's canonical location, roles and current matching counts.
parts.reason: F-RELATE and F-FIND require accurate structural context; charter section 5 M3 and the owner's encoding decision forbid using class colour as identity.
requirements: Resolve cell picks to canonical IDs from current geometry, independent of repeated class colours.
Update hover details when state, work roles or filters change even if the pointer stays on the same cell.
Selection and hover must not assign a target, select a Grip, move the camera or execute a turn.

parts.purpose: Center a geometric view on the canonical cell the solver explicitly selected.
parts.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 retain explicit camera movement, while charter section 5 D8 folds the old main viewport into the two linked views.
requirements: Invoke a camera command with a validated canonical cell, preserving state, protection and solving roles.
Make the command keyboard reachable and avoid synchronous engine queries on the UI thread.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Choose and understand the ordered frame that gives a selected cap's legal turns their fixed meaning.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow section 4.3 require stable Grip/Twist meanings; F-CHECK needs exact frame correspondence rather than colour matching.
requirements: Expose the legal proper ordered frames with exact old/new corner correspondence and the resulting legal Twist axes.
Require an explicit frame change against the current cap, bank and prior-frame revision; clear held input and invalidate affected reviews.
Explain the frame with the shared glossary and encoding, without inferring it from camera orientation or relabelling the model.

rows.purpose: Describe intended block achievements and choose the work that must be preserved.
rows.reason: Solving-workflow section 3.3 separates block progress conditions from protection, so F-COMPOSE and F-PROTECT need distinct decisions within this coarse unit.

parts.purpose: Declare and edit exact Home or referenced block requirements, including placement-only requirements.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-TARGET follow solving-workflow section 3.3: a block is an explicit achievement whose membership, reference and conditions the solver chooses.
requirements: Distinguish identity, destination, exact slots/orientation and placement-only conditions; completed, selected and protected are separate facts.
Referenced blocks require one verified common reference and must not imply an unproved rigid transport.
Transport only desired requirements with the solver's finite legal reference word; leave existing protection fixed and invalidate the operation review.
Current-state capture must require acknowledged actual inspection, never a forecast token.

parts.purpose: Capture or release exact, position-only and whole-orbit preservation requirements explicitly.
parts.reason: F-PROTECT and solving-workflow sections 2 and 3.3 require preservation at the solver's chosen scope, including the captured state of an unfinished protected orbit.
requirements: Keep identity, position, exact-label and block constraints distinct; releasing one constraint must not silently release another.
Reject forecast-based capture on every input route, recheck the protection revision before saving and invalidate any prior review.
Keep global protection visible under all filters and across orbit switches; completion-triggered protection must not undo a manual unlock on unchanged state.
Never unlock work automatically to make a macro applicable.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Tune geometric visibility and rendering for a readable, comfortable view of the work.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 preserve tunable themes and legible geometry, while sections 2 and 4 replace retained display controls and keep the full-detail renderer gate binding.
requirements: Use validated display ranges and shared theme tokens, preserving picking, role/status meanings, accessibility alternatives and geometric truth.
Framework visibility, size, lighting, projection and optional motion sampling must never change labels, model identity, analysis scope or generator availability.
Every shipped theme's most expensive scene must pass the full-detail renderer gate; optional motion detail must not substitute for that evidence.
Apply and recover display preferences independently of puzzle state and keep display commands keyboard reachable.

rows.purpose: Define the interactive work scope and reference visibility using explicit composable piece filters.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and solving-workflow section 4.3 preserve filters while keeping full mechanical analysis, interactive work and noninteractive reference display separate.
requirements: Validate the entire Boolean filter and its composition before application, retain rejected input and show current counts and replacement scope.
Distinguish a live query, following fixed identities and watching fixed positions; do not silently substitute one for another.
Hidden buffers may remain noninteractive references; making them pickable or twistable is a separate explicit action.
Never reduce the 259,800-label analysis or hide protection conflicts and complete-operation collateral.

rows.purpose: Inspect the committed state and exact predicted state at each boundary of the solver's operation.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and solving-workflow sections 2 and 4.1 require boundary forecasts to remain distinct from staged permission and committed state.
requirements: Simulate Prepare, Macro and Cleanup in chronological order on all labels and bind the displayed forecast to current state, workspace, protection and frame revisions.
Label forecasts as predictions and report an unchecked protected prefix as unchecked, never safe.
Inspection must not stage or execute; an executed or edited draft cannot retain old forecast authority.
Share current and target frame anchors between the two views and expose full collateral even when regions are filtered.

rows.purpose: Edit ordered operation phases and choose how input and intermediate protection are interpreted.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE edits the operation, while F-CHECK chooses its protection policy; solving-workflow section 4.1 separately defines draft/live input and Net/Strict checking.

parts.purpose: Enter, reorder and save the solver's finite legal steps in Prepare, Macro or Cleanup.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE follows solving-workflow section 4: the solver composes the three phases and chooses the destination of each draft edit.
requirements: Preserve chronological source-to-destination order and validate complete finite legal words before an atomic draft save.
Retain local edits after validation, stale-context or save failure and provide workspace undo; unadded input must not vanish.
Saving a phase must recheck its source revision and invalidate all operation reviews, forecasts and execution permission.

parts.purpose: Choose explicitly whether subsequent turns edit a draft or change the live puzzle.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE preserve the draft/live distinction of solving-workflow section 4.1.
requirements: Display the input destination at every turn route; changing it must not itself issue a turn.
Draft turns change only the selected phase, while every live turn independently checks active protection and commits a complete operation.
Clear held input on a destination change and never treat future Cleanup as permission for a live protected prefix.

parts.purpose: Choose Net preservation at the complete endpoint or Strict preservation after every primitive.
parts.reason: F-CHECK and F-PROTECT follow solving-workflow section 2: temporary motion inside a complete macro is different from a checked safe prefix.
requirements: Name and explain Net and Strict using the shared mathematical glossary; check the full operation including all hidden collateral.
Changing policy invalidates the review and execution permission; unexamined intermediate steps remain visibly unchecked.
Keep goal progress and legal/protected execution permission separate.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Prepare, review, execute and recover explicit operations while retaining control of analysis jobs.
rows.reason: Solving-workflow sections 4 and 4.1 separate drafting, permission, explicit execution and recovery; command-table section 1 also gives job control its own responsibility.

parts.purpose: Start a new draft or deliberately reuse retained steps and reach their editing controls.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE preserve the solver's recipes, with a fresh review on reuse under solving-workflow section 4.1.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Preserve fixed ordered phases on reuse, require explicit replacement of unsaved work and invalidate old permission.
Executed steps must remain visibly historical until an explicit New or Reuse action creates a draft.
Reaching or hiding controls must retain context and leave both linked views usable.

parts.purpose: Review and stage the complete predicted effect, inspect protection conflicts or withdraw the preview.
parts.reason: F-CHECK and F-PROTECT require full-effect review, and solving-workflow section 4.1 makes a current preview the basis for explicit execution.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Bind review and preview to state, workspace and protection revisions, full-state hash, model identity and macro/frame versions.
Show all 259,800-label effects, buffer/frame changes and endpoint or Strict conflicts, including filtered-out regions.
A goal may be unmet while execution is legal; score, evidence and permission must stay separate.
Cancel only preview authority while retaining the draft; comparison overlays cannot authorize execution or become committed state.

parts.purpose: Execute a current reviewed operation explicitly and undo or redo journalled work safely.
parts.reason: F-EXECUTE and charter section 5 E4 require explicit commits and recovery; solving-workflow sections 4 and 7 forbid execution without the solver's action.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Recheck preview revisions, full-state hash and all protected constraints immediately before commit and apply the finite witness chronologically with full collateral.
Use one transactional journal commit and a durable command identity; retries must not apply the operation twice.
Keep accepted commit/undo/redo receipts separate from refresh failure and expose applied-but-stale display without encouraging repetition.
Undo and redo must preserve history and current global protection rules and resolve work identities afresh.

parts.purpose: Stop an active analysis and know whether cancellation has completed.
parts.reason: F-CHECK and F-PLATFORM require cancellable jobs and a responsive shell under command-table sections 1 and 2.
requirements: X-02: Keep commit, undo, redo and snapshot/status latency bounded as checkpoint history grows; read separately indexed checkpoint metadata and page checkpoint lists without scanning label blobs on the interactive path.
Run long checks away from the UI thread and distinguish requested cancellation, acknowledged cancellation, accepted commit and unknown outcome.
Keep conflicting inputs blocked until job/finalizer completion is acknowledged; cancellation must not queue another mutation.
Retain drafts and any accepted receipts, and explain the continuation after a failed or unacknowledged stop.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately. X-02 is attached to the broad lifecycle row, so each retained part carries the shared status-path requirement.

rows.purpose: Understand an operation's exact findings and inspect the objects that explain them.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and charter section 5 S4 require a readable witness and complete effect; solving-workflow section 4.1 separates goal progress from protection and execution permission.
requirements: Show endpoint goal results, all protection conflicts, Strict-prefix evidence and computable reasons as distinct facts.
Link each reason to its canonical objects and actual full-operation scope; reject evidence from another revision or work binding.
Replace the fixed three-reason text presentation with access to all relevant findings, using the shared graphical grammar and exact details on inspection.
Explain missing or unverified evidence explicitly; a failed check is never a low score or a suggested solving macro.

rows.purpose: Apply an explicit legal reference to the solver's work and save a deliberately requested variant of the solver's macro.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-REUSE allow the solver's own reference and template operations under solving-workflow section 7; charter section 2 preserves finite legal witnesses and their complete action.
requirements: Validate the finite legal reference R, including the empty identity word, and explain its ordered-frame meaning.
A requested R variant must use the explicitly selected solver-owned macro revision and the chronological word inverse(R), Macro, R, preserving every collateral label.
Recheck the source and reference before saving; save, selection, insertion and execution remain separate explicit actions.
Never choose a reference or synthesize a solving macro from a target/residual; setup search is a separately permitted preparation tool.

rows.purpose: Declare the intended achievement against which the solver's operation will be analysed.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE, F-CHECK and F-ENDGAME use explicit work goals; solving-workflow section 4.1 says preparation must not be blocked for failing to improve a goal.
requirements: Express placement, orientation, buffer, block and exact orbit goals using precise identity/position/frame conditions.
Report met, unmet, missing-input and unverified goals independently from evidence and permission.
Changing a goal invalidates the review; the tool analyses the solver's operation rather than choosing a macro to achieve it.

rows.purpose: Reach macro selection, preparation and protection tools without losing the current solving context.
rows.reason: F-MACRO, F-COMPOSE and F-PROTECT are adjacent steps of solving-workflow section 4; charter section 5 requires a new integrated experience rather than retaining the Solve-window pages.
requirements: Make every surviving action reachable by command ID and keyboard with one shared target, buffers, block and protection context.
Keep operation and residual summaries embedded in the linked views; expanded tools must not introduce a third geometric view.
Preserve drafts on tool transitions and invalidate review authority only when its actual inputs change.

rows.purpose: Find, use and record the solver's own fixed macros.
rows.reason: F-MACRO chooses or records an existing word, while F-COMPOSE explicitly inserts it into a draft; solving-workflow section 4 separates those actions.

parts.purpose: Find and inspect a deliberately selected existing macro and its exact bound effect.
parts.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain analysis of the solver's own macros under solving-workflow section 7, with the orbit-and-use organization of section 6.
requirements: F-02: Deliver one macro insertion or focused command activation per deliberate press; held Enter or Space must not repeat a mutating action.
F-03: Route Enter to the focused list's declared activation through the command layer; editors and modal contexts must not lose the event to a global pre-filter.
F-05: Validate catalogue/candidate evidence once per relevant model, state, macro or protection revision, never per painted macro row.
Show orbit, use, fixed recipe, canonical ID, revision, complete collateral and current applicability without conflating them.
A search must not silently replace a hidden selection, insert a macro or pick a correction for the solver.
Catalogue inspection and return to work must preserve context, and stale source/body evidence must be withdrawn.

parts.purpose: Append or replace a phase with the exact macro the solver explicitly selected.
parts.reason: F-COMPOSE and solving-workflow sections 4 and 4.1 require deliberate phase composition and a fresh review of the whole result.
requirements: F-02: Deliver one macro insertion or focused command activation per deliberate press; held Enter or Space must not repeat a mutating action.
F-03: Route Enter to the focused list's declared activation through the command layer; editors and modal contexts must not lose the event to a global pre-filter.
F-05: Validate catalogue/candidate evidence once per relevant model, state, macro or protection revision, never per painted macro row.
Copy only the selected fixed revision into the named phase, require explicit replacement scope and retain workspace undo.
Insertion must invalidate review and preview authority and never stage or execute the operation.
Retain recorded-scramble provenance on rejected insertion and update it only after an accepted draft change.

parts.purpose: Record a solver-entered finite legal word as a named reusable macro.
parts.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE are expressly allowed by solving-workflow section 7; the program analyses the supplied macro instead of generating a solution.
requirements: Validate the whole concrete recipe and retain its finite legal witness, chronological action and full collateral before saving.
Use stable canonical identity and versioned recipes; keep user labels and notes separate from proof claims.
Saving must not select, insert or execute, and rejected input must remain available for correction.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately. The coarse catalogue row covers browsing and insertion; concrete macro creation has its own fine row.

rows.purpose: Organize, validate, annotate and exchange the solver's recorded macro collection.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE use catalogue discovery, evidence, metadata and file exchange as different purposes; command-table section 1 keeps each mutation on one command path.

parts.purpose: Find recorded macros by checked effect, orbit, use and user metadata.
parts.reason: F-MACRO and solving-workflow section 6 require a macro base organized by orbit and use, without a program-chosen solving macro.
requirements: Distinguish checked action facts, inferred likely use and unchecked records; filters must not turn inference into verification.
Validate compound facets and preserve explicit selection; resetting pending facets must not silently apply them.
Filtering may explain candidate relevance but must not select, emit or execute a solution.

parts.purpose: Check the complete effects of existing macro records and see which records remain unchecked.
parts.reason: F-CHECK and F-MACRO allow analysis of the solver's macros under solving-workflow section 7; charter section 2 requires all collateral to remain part of the result.
requirements: Use bounded cancellable analysis with explicit coverage counts and resource-limit results; a batch limit must not hide unchecked records.
Bind results to model and macro revisions and relevant state/protection inputs, reusing valid evidence rather than checking during paint.
Classification must not choose or generate a correction macro and cannot certify a complete operation's intermediate protection.

parts.purpose: Name, annotate, tag and pin the solver's saved macros without changing their mathematical recipes.
parts.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE require understandable durable records; command-table section 1 puts metadata changes in the workspace transaction path.
requirements: Preserve the canonical recipe identity and revision on metadata-only edits and update all affected views from the workspace revision.
Retain unsaved input on errors and expose workspace undo for accepted edits; a pin is not selection or protection.

parts.purpose: Exchange explicitly selected macro records through checked local library files.
parts.reason: F-REUSE and command-table sections 1 and 2 require checked file scope, explicit application and durable workspace writes.
requirements: Export exact canonical recipes and identities atomically; inspect bounded versioned input and report new, identical and conflicting entries before importing.
Validate the complete import and recheck its digest and workspace basis before an atomic apply; conflicts must not cause a partial import.
Keep local metadata for identical records, ignore imported assertions of verification and recompute proof evidence for the matching model.
Import must not select or execute a macro.

Show canonical buffer/auxiliary roles, exact slot actions, witness, full collateral and certificate/evidence status for the selected revision.

Selection and inspection must not insert or execute; require a fresh whole-operation protection review before explicit execution.

rows.purpose: Copy exact addresses, configure useful caps, access geometry, preserve checkpoints and open practice evidence.

parts.purpose: Copy a complete canonical identity or mathematical address for the acknowledged inspected object.

Recheck the bank, actual inspected piece and retained frame context before saving, clear held input and invalidate affected review authority.

parts.purpose: Access the actual full-model geometric state while keeping the current solving context.

Maintain the full model under visibility filters and keep forecast overlays visibly separate from actual state.

parts.purpose: Save named recovery points and deliberately restore a selected checkpoint without losing recoverable work.
parts.reason: F-PROTECT and F-SESSION follow solving-workflow section 4.2 and charter section 5 E4, with transactional recoverable persistence under AGENTS.md.
requirements: List checkpoints using bounded metadata queries and show exact restore scope before an explicit command.
Restore through transactional journal/recovery semantics, revalidate protection, retain current preferences and keep a recovery checkpoint.
Resolve identities again, invalidate reviews and retain accepted restore receipts even when refresh fails.

parts.purpose: Open a clearly labelled full-model practice fixture for learning and competence checks.

requirements: Initialize only a fresh clearly labelled full-model practice session, preserving the user's ongoing solve and recovery data.
Use an explicit finite legal fixture witness and the same command/protection path; do not discard locks or bypass protected-orbit checks.
Keep fixture initialization distinct from a human solve, automatic correction and completion rewards; no regression fixture may run during normal startup.
Measure competence separately from time and retain any accepted initialization receipt across refresh failure.

rows.notes: The coarse Claude row spans these purposes and is repeated in the applicable parts; the fine Codex rows identify each action separately.

rows.purpose: Read exact residuals, inspect the last result and deliberately choose a following orbit.

parts.purpose: See the orbit's exact remaining placement, orientation, buffer and frame conditions.

Report nonbuffer Home errors, buffer occupants, orientation errors, unknown frames and exact completion independently.
Distinguish permitted nonidentity residuals from solved state and diagnose impossible residuals as provenance/mapping/certificate problems.
Bind residuals and invariant certificates to the actual state and model, showing stale or missing evidence explicitly.
Embed the summary in the linked views without generating or automatically choosing a correction.

parts.purpose: Inspect the actual changes and protected damage recorded for the last committed operation.

requirements: X-01: Preserve identity-bearing asset and proof bytes across Windows checkouts and packaged sources, verify their digests before use and show a mismatched proof as stale rather than verified.
Display before/after position and orientation facts from the durable journal receipt, never substitute a prediction for the result.
Tie changed-position inspection to the current journal head and resolve canonical IDs afresh; stale receipts remain historical.
Show all protected damage and buffer changes, even outside the current work filter.

parts.purpose: Choose an unfinished orbit after checking the current orbit's exact completion.
parts.reason: F-TARGET and solving-workflow section 4.2 require suggestions with reasons and a solver choice, with locked Next taking priority.
requirements: X-01: Preserve identity-bearing asset and proof bytes across Windows checkouts and packaged sources, verify their digests before use and show a mismatched proof as stale rather than verified.
Use exact completion and the certified collateral-dependent order, respecting the solver's locked Next and explaining alternatives.
Switch only after an explicit choice, save per-orbit drafts atomically and retain current global protection.
Residual work without candidates must open endgame inspection, not trigger a generated solution or automatic orbit switch.

Page cycles and edges completely with stable keyboard focus; choosing an inspection orbit must not change the working orbit.

requirements: D-03: Consult the revision- and source-bound After-view cache before simulating a forecast; paging unchanged cycle and edge indexes must reuse that forecast.
Refresh only when the selected source or relevant model, state, workspace, protection, frame or filter inputs change, using asynchronous coalesced work.

Report the current journal head, source/provenance, operation and scramble counts and timer from authoritative receipts.
Resume drafts and choices, resolve identities again and invalidate execution permission while keeping current global protection.
Avoid redundant work on unchanged revisions and never treat a refresh failure as failure of an accepted session action.

requirements: C-04: Preserve the recorded scramble seed, word and provenance when a draft edit or request is rejected; only a successfully accepted replacement may change its provenance.

Validate before database writes, retain current preferences, personal key sets and macros, and preserve a recovery checkpoint for the previous state.
Apply the full model transactionally through the command layer, invalidate reviews and preserve accepted receipts across refresh failure.
Do not blanket-lock a newly solved/reset session or award human-solve completion for resetting to Home.

parts.purpose: Reset work presentation or camera defaults without discarding puzzle history or personal tools.

requirements: C-04: Preserve the recorded scramble seed, word and provenance when a draft edit or request is rejected; only a successfully accepted replacement may change its provenance.
Separate clearing roles/drafts from resetting camera/display defaults and show the exact affected workspace scope.
Keep committed labels, journal, current protection, personal key sets, macros and recovery data intact.
Invalidate only reviews whose work inputs changed, clear held input and keep both linked views usable.

parts.purpose: Stage a reproducible legal scramble that the solver can inspect and explicitly apply.

requirements: C-04: Preserve the recorded scramble seed, word and provenance when a draft edit or request is rejected; only a successfully accepted replacement may change its provenance.
Retain the seed, finite chronological legal word, model identity and recorded-scramble provenance independently of display filters.
Require explicit consent before replacing existing steps or preview and show a fresh complete protection review before execution.
Scramble generation must not execute by itself, masquerade as solution work or weaken existing protection.
Offer clearly labelled isolated practice without touching the ongoing solve; declare resource limits rather than inheriting arbitrary 0.4 lengths.

requirements: C-04: Preserve the recorded scramble seed, word and provenance when a draft edit or request is rejected; only a successfully accepted replacement may change its provenance.
Make timer scope, running/paused state and interruption behaviour explicit; timer actions must not issue puzzle turns.
Keep attempt time, assistance/provenance and competence/progress facts separate and store metrics locally without uploads.
Settle the timer's journal versus workspace ownership and undo class in the command table before implementing its persistence.

parts.purpose: Inspect, import, save and export verified journal work through recoverable local records.

requirements: C-04: Preserve the recorded scramble seed, word and provenance when a draft edit or request is rejected; only a successfully accepted replacement may change its provenance.
Validate the complete bounded record, model identity, chronological witness replay and export/import limits before any write; exports must be importable by the matching format.
Bind explicit import confirmation to the inspected file digest and current session basis; import atomically with a recovery checkpoint while retaining current preferences.
Publish verified bytes atomically and keep accepted import/export receipts separate from refresh failure or unknown outcomes.

Require an exact committed-state check of every required identity, position, orientation and sticker, including fixed structures; empty candidates or matching colours are insufficient.

Keep rewards small and in place at the owner's three occasions plus the whole-puzzle moment; do not unlock functions, themes or permissions.
Undo withdraws current achievement and pending celebration while keeping already unlocked explanations and user-saved macros; reopening a report is not new completion.

rows.purpose: Save and reuse the solver's fixed work method while comparing its saved inputs with the current work.

requirements: Save fixed roles, phase recipes, reference, goal and macro versions, retaining stable IDs and exact details for inspection/copy.
Compare saved and current inputs, show mismatches and protection conflicts without silently retargeting or rebinding the method.
Loading requires explicit consent bound to a fresh comparison and keeps current inputs/global protection; any reused method needs a fresh complete review.
Refresh comparison data asynchronously and retain the local work after rejection, cancellation or stale evidence; no selection, insertion or execution is automatic.

rows.purpose: Review Grip input and discover the tools needed to prepare a legal turn in one shared workspace.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-LEARN retain Grip review, while charter sections 4 and 5 and the owner's one-entry decision replace the separate G1 review layout.
requirements: Expose current cap, ordered frame, input policy, protection and command availability without retaining a separate native mode or entry door.
Keep every action keyboard reachable through the shared command table and link its exact meaning to Global/Local and the onscreen keyboard.
Use task-led optional coaching and soft disclosure; review controls must never apply a turn merely by being opened.

rows.purpose: Adjust or dismiss optional work surfaces while preserving their content and recoverable placement.

requirements: Persist accepted optional-surface placement/visibility without stale saves overwriting newer preferences and restore usable bounds on current displays.
Keep Global and Local visible together; closing an optional tool must retain its work and return focus predictably.
Support keyboard routes, display scaling and monitor changes without altering mechanical state or leaving held turn input active.

rows.purpose: Leave a local editor or inspection safely while knowing whether any requested change was accepted.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-SESSION need predictable cancellation; command-table section 1 and charter section 5 E4 distinguish local dismissal from an accepted transaction.
requirements: Discard only unsaved local input when explicitly cancelled, protecting valuable edits with clear scope and preserving committed workspace changes.
For an in-flight request, follow the declared wait/stop/outcome protocol; dismissal must not roll back or conceal an accepted save or import.
Return focus to the originating context, clear held input and keep keyboard cancellation separate from puzzle commands.

rows.purpose: Navigate controls and activate the focused action reliably from the keyboard.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 E5 require every action to be keyboard reachable; command-table section 2 makes context and repeat policy part of the command contract.
requirements: F-02: Deliver one macro insertion or focused command activation per deliberate press; held Enter or Space must not repeat a mutating action.
F-03: Route Enter to the focused list's declared activation through the command layer; editors and modal contexts must not lose the event to a global pre-filter.
Use visible predictable focus order and context-specific activation with one command dispatch route; never invoke retained hidden accelerators.
Give editors, modal tools and IME their keystrokes and suppress held-key repeats for commits and macro insertion.
Keep physical, onscreen and focused-control activation equivalent under availability, busy, stale and protection gates.
Verify focus routing and repeat behaviour with appropriate input fixtures before claiming native input correctness.

rows.purpose: Close an active work surface or exit the application without losing accepted work or leaving owned resources running.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM require recoverable interruption and orderly ownership under AGENTS.md; charter section 4 does not inherit the old process split.
requirements: Distinguish closing a tool from leaving the application; retain durable commits, recovery checkpoints and saved context before final shutdown.
Resolve in-flight outcomes and stop/cancel jobs in order, clearing held input and disposing owned resources.
If a local engine process is owned, use EngineProcess authenticated health, graceful shutdown and parent-pipe recovery rather than inheriting raw retained-host process control.
Preserve the fixed idle/trickling-request shutdown regression requirement and never start regression fixtures during normal exit.

rows.purpose: Adjust the space available to linked geometric work while retaining readable controls and precise picking.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and charter section 5 D5, D8 and anti-goal 11 require dense readable views whose scaling preserves the relationship between the frame and puzzle.
requirements: Keep both Global and Local usable and linked under resizing and high-DPI scaling without choosing a 1.0 layout here.
Provide a keyboard command for any adjustable allocation and clamp it to readable, operable bounds.
Recompute display/picking geometry from view state without changing labels, roles or camera-independent key meanings.

rows.purpose: Understand startup or runtime failures and recover work using a clear next action.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM rely on actionable errors; charter section 5 E4, E6 and D2 replace the old fatal-message presentation.
requirements: State what happened, why and what the user can do, distinguishing rejected, cancelled, applied-but-stale and unknown outcomes.
Keep accepted receipts and recovery checkpoints available; a recoverable operation error must not be escalated to application exit.
Put local diagnostics behind a narrow platform boundary and do not publish credentials, user data, personal logs or raw machine paths.
Display errors asynchronously and offer retry only when its command identity and outcome make retry safe.

rows.purpose: Read the complete current work context, operation outcome and protection status behind compact summaries.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK require shared context, and charter section 5 M3, E6 and D8 preserve exact evidence and errors in the two linked views.
requirements: Expose full canonical identity/position, Current/Next, buffer and protection details by keyboard focus as well as pointer inspection.
Keep displayed context on one authoritative revision and refresh details when inputs change, even with unchanged hover or focus.
Distinguish evidence, score, permission, current progress and accepted outcome; abbreviated text must not conceal stale-state or protection failures.
Use the shared graphical grammar and human-reviewed English wording; exact IDs, glossary terms and actionable error details remain accessible.
